title: Migration 018 drops a constrained column without dropping its constraints

evidence.quote:
if "digest_id" in existing:
        with op.batch_alter_table("podcast_episodes") as batch_op:
            batch_op.drop_index("ix_podcast_episodes_digest_id")
            batch_op.drop_column("digest_id")

reasoning: Revision 014 creates a foreign key and a named unique constraint on podcast_episodes.digest_id. Revision 018 removes only the secondary index before dropping digest_id. In Alembic SQLite batch mode, named constraints can be carried into the rebuilt table unless explicitly dropped, so the rebuild can fail or attempt to recreate constraints that reference a removed column. That would block existing deployments from upgrading past 017.
reproduction: Create a SQLite database at revision 017 with the podcast_episodes schema from 014, then run revision 018. The batch table rebuild attempts to remove digest_id while constraints from 014 still reference it.
recommendation: In 018, explicitly drop the digest_id unique constraint and foreign key during the batch operation, or replace the batch operation with an explicit create-copy-rename rebuild that defines only the desired post-018 constraints.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature includes no migration tests. The existing podcast API tests exercise the current model schema, not an Alembic upgrade from a 017 database containing the old digest_id constraints.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an Alembic migration test that builds a SQLite DB through revision 017, inserts a podcast_episodes row, upgrades to 018/head, and asserts the upgrade succeeds, digest_id is absent, digest_ids contains the old ID, and no constraints reference digest_id.
minimumFixScope: Update alembic/versions/018_podcast_multi_digest.py and add one migration regression test.
